/-!
# Erdős Problem 491

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/491](https://www.erdosproblems.com/491)
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, *Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved*.
  (1982), 59--79.
- [Wi70] E. Wirsing, A characterization of $\log n$ as an additive arithmetic function.
  Symposia Math. (1970), 45-57.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos491

/--
Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be an additive function (so that $f(ab) = f(a) + f(b)$
whenever $(a, b) = 1$). If $|f(n+1) - f(n)| < c$ for some constant $c$ and all $n$, then must
there exist some $c'$ such that $f(n) = c' \log n + O(1)$?

A question of Erdős [Er61, p.237; Er82e, p.65], who had proved that $f(n) = c' \log n$ under the
stronger hypotheses $f(n+1) - f(n) = o(1)$ or $f(n+1) \ge f(n)$. The answer is yes, proved by
Wirsing [Wi70]. See also `erdos_897.variants.log_growth`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos491.lean#L34"]
theorem erdos_491 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (f : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ᵉ (a > 0) (b > 0), a.Coprime b → f (a * b) = f a + f b) →
      (∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, |f (n + 1) - f n| < C) →
      ∃ c : ℝ, (fun n : ℕ ↦ f n - c * Real.log n) =O[atTop] (fun _ : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos491

reformulations.difference: The gap bound includes n = 0, whereas the source concerns arithmetic functions on positive integers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The bound is existential. Given a bound C for positive n, replacing it by max C (|f 1 - f 0| + 1) also bounds the single extra gap at zero. Conversely, an all-natural bound restricts to positive integers. The value at zero does not affect the atTop conclusion. This equivalence was proved as gap_bound_zero_iff in the scratch file.

reformulations.difference: The source's decomposition f(n) = c log n + g(n), with bounded error g (explicitly additive in the 1982 survey), is expressed as a big-O condition on f(n) - c log n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For real sequences, =O[atTop] 1 means an eventual absolute bound, equivalent to a uniform bound on positive integers because there are only finitely many exceptional initial values. Set g(n) = f(n) - c log n. Its arithmetic additivity follows from that of f and log(ab) = log a + log b for positive a,b. Conversely, any such bounded decomposition gives the stated big-O condition. Strict and weak existential bounds are interchangeable by enlarging the constant. The equivalence was proved as conclusion_iff_bounded_additive_decomposition.
